description: Remove oil stains from a driveway in 1 evening: clay litter overnight, then dish soap on asphalt or an alkaline degreaser on concrete. Steps for each.
dek: Remove oil stains from a driveway in 1 evening: clay litter overnight, then dish soap on asphalt or an alkaline degreaser on concrete.
intro: To remove oil stains from a driveway, cover the spot with clay kitty litter, grind it in and leave it overnight, then scrub what is left for about 30 minutes: dish soap or a water-based degreaser on asphalt, a strong alkaline degreaser on concrete. A fresh spill usually disappears in one evening that way.

The surface changes everything. Asphalt is held together by a petroleum binder, so anything strong enough to dissolve motor oil can dissolve the pavement too. Concrete shrugs off strong cleaners but soaks oil deep into its pores. This guide walks through the first hour after a spill, separate methods for blacktop and concrete, pavers and sealed surfaces, other car fluids and how to stop the next stain.
quickAnswer: Soak up free oil with plain clay litter ground into the surface and left overnight, then scrub with a cleaner matched to the surface and rinse away from the street. On asphalt use only water-based cleaners, never solvents. On concrete, use an alkaline degreaser and expect a weeks-old stain to need two or three rounds; judge each round only when the slab is fully dry.

blocks.p: Never hose a fresh puddle, and never put solvents on blacktop. A fresh spill usually lifts completely with absorbent and one cleaning. A concrete stain that survives two full rounds has moved deeper than a degreaser can reach, and the methods in our guide on [how to get oil out of concrete](/how-to-get-oil-out-of-concrete/) take over from there.

sections.h: Is Your Driveway Asphalt or Concrete, and Why Does It Matter?

blocks.p: The same cleaner can help one surface and harm the other, so check the pavement before you buy anything. Plenty of driveways are both: a concrete apron at the street with blacktop up to the garage, or a concrete garage slab meeting an asphalt drive right at the door. Those transitions are where cars stop, so they are where oil collects.

Asphalt is black or dark gray, gives slightly on a hot day and shows bare stone after a few years of weathering. Concrete is light gray and rigid with a broom texture or smooth troweled face. Stamped and colored concrete still behave like concrete. Brick and concrete pavers are their own group because of the sand joints between units.

blocks.h3: Why oil damages asphalt but only stains concrete

blocks.p: Asphalt pavement is stone glued with bitumen, a heavy petroleum product. Motor oil, gasoline and solvent degreasers are close chemical relatives of that glue and soften it. A spill left on blacktop for a week can leave a tacky spot that crumbles under a tire. Concrete is a mineral surface full of tiny capillary pores. Oil does not weaken it, but it travels down and outward through those pores, which is why old concrete stains are so stubborn.

blocks.p: A wet, glossy spot is fresh and mostly on top. A dull, dark patch that no longer feels slick has worked its way in. Fresh stains are a cleanup job; old stains on concrete are a restoration project.

sections.h: What Should You Do in the First Hour After an Oil Spill?

blocks.p: Cover it with dry absorbent, grind it in and leave it. On concrete, the first 30 to 60 minutes decide most of the outcome; on asphalt, speed also limits how much binder the oil softens.

blocks.h3: Do not reach for the hose

blocks.p: Water does not dissolve oil. It floats it, spreads it over a wider area and pushes it into cracks and toward the storm drain, where automotive fluids are prohibited in most places.

Plain, non-clumping, unscented clay kitty litter is cheap and sold everywhere. Granular shop absorbents such as Oil-Dri work the same way and pull a little harder. Sawdust, cornmeal and baking soda work in a pinch but hold less oil per pound. Spread a layer about half an inch deep and an inch past the wet edge.

This is the step most people skip. Grinding with a shoe or a brick crushes the granules into finer particles, which multiplies their surface area and lets them reach into the pavement texture. On asphalt, twist rather than scrape so you do not loosen stone. Leave it a few hours at least, overnight if possible, then sweep it into a bag. Small amounts usually go in household trash, but check local hazardous waste rules.

That is a good second step once the absorbent is up. Squeeze a generous line of grease-cutting dish soap onto the spot, add a splash of water, scrub for a couple of minutes with a stiff nylon brush, wait 15 minutes and rinse with a bucket. On a fresh spill, absorbent plus soap often leaves nothing visible on either surface.

ul: Wear the gloves and eye protection the cleaner label calls for.
Never pour gasoline on a stain or try to burn oil off.
Rinse toward lawn or gravel where allowed, or collect water with a wet vacuum.
With gasoline spills, ventilate, keep ignition sources away and never vacuum the fuel.
Keep pets and children away from coolant spills until the area is clean.

sections.h: How Do You Remove Oil Stains From an Asphalt Driveway?

blocks.p: Use only water-based cleaners, keep contact times short and keep the brush and pressure gentle. That rules out anything sold as a solvent degreaser, citrus solvent, mineral spirits, brake cleaner or carburetor cleaner, and the old trick of burning oil off with gasoline.

ol: Absorb free oil as above and sweep it up.
Dampen the area lightly so cleaner does not soak straight into dry pavement.
Apply a water-based degreaser labeled safe for asphalt, a microbial cleaner or a strong dish soap solution.
Work it in with a stiff nylon brush and moderate pressure; avoid wire brushes, which tear loose fine aggregate.
Let it dwell 5 to 10 minutes while keeping it wet, then rinse with a hose on a fan setting.
Repeat once or twice rather than leaving cleaner on for a long time.

blocks.p: If a label mentions only concrete, test it on an out-of-the-way corner and check for softening before treating the main stain.

blocks.h3: Do enzyme cleaners work on asphalt?

blocks.p: Yes, and they suit it well, because enzyme and microbial products break hydrocarbons down without solvents. They need a day or more and must stay damp, but they leave the binder alone. Owners commonly report a faint shadow fading over the following week.
On sound asphalt at moderate settings, yes. Use a 25 or 40 degree tip, hold it at least 12 inches away and keep it moving. A narrow tip close up blasts out aggregate and leaves a pale, rough patch.

Push a screwdriver into the stain. If it sinks in more easily than in clean pavement, the binder is damaged. Clean what you can, let it cure a few days, then brush on an asphalt oil spot primer before sealing, because sealer will not bond to oily patches. If it crumbles, cut it out and fill with cold patch. Our [asphalt driveway sealer reviews](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) note which products include a primer step.

sections.h: How Do You Remove Oil Stains From a Concrete Driveway?

blocks.p: Absorb, then scrub with a concentrated alkaline degreaser and rinse hard. Concrete tolerates much stronger chemistry than asphalt, but it also holds stains deeper, especially on a broom-finished or weathered slab.

A concentrated alkaline degreaser such as Oil Eater, Purple Power or Zep Driveway and Concrete Cleaner does the work. Mix it at the strongest heavy-grease dilution the label allows. Dampen the concrete slightly, apply, and scrub hard with a stiff nylon or polypropylene deck brush on a pole. Let it dwell for the label time, typically 5 to 15 minutes, and do not let it dry in the sun.

A pressure washer with a 15 or 25 degree tip held 8 to 12 inches away works well on sound concrete. Hot water helps a great deal because heat thins oil; with a cold-water machine, a second degreaser application stands in for the heat. Aim the rinse at lawn or gravel, or pick up the wash water with a shop vacuum.

blocks.h3: Gone while wet, back the next day?

blocks.p: Wet concrete darkens evenly and hides what is left. Wait 24 to 48 hours before judging. A weeks-old stain usually needs two or three rounds. If it is fainter but still there after two full rounds, switching methods beats a fourth pass with the same product. A poultice pulls oil up from deeper in the slab and an enzyme cleaner digests what a degreaser leaves; our [best oil stain remover for concrete](/best-oil-stain-remover-for-concrete/) roundup sorts those products by stain age.

blocks.h3: What about muriatic acid or bleach?

blocks.p: Leave both out. Acid etches the cement paste and brightens the concrete around the spot without dissolving oil, so you get a clean ring around an unchanged stain. Bleach lightens leaves and mildew, not petroleum.

sections.h: How Do You Clean Oil Off Pavers and Sealed or Stamped Concrete?

blocks.p: Start with the mildest cleaner and step up slowly, because the sealer or joint sand can be damaged before the stain is gone.

A good penetrating sealer slows oil, so fresh spills often come up more completely than on bare concrete. Film-forming acrylic sealers, common on stamped and colored slabs, can be softened by solvents and some strong degreasers. Begin with dish soap and a soft brush, move to a water-based degreaser at light dilution and only then try a stronger mix. A hazy or white patch afterward means the cleaner has affected the sealer. If oil has crept under a worn acrylic film, that section has to be stripped, cleaned and resealed.

Oil runs off a paver face and soaks into the joint sand, which then keeps re-staining the edges. Treat both the paver and the joint with absorbent or a poultice, rinse at low pressure so you do not wash out the sand, and refill joints once dry. A badly stained paver can simply be lifted and flipped or replaced. Once clean, a [paver sealer](/best-paver-sealer/) buys time to blot the next drip.

sections.h: Is the Spot on Your Driveway Oil, Transmission Fluid, Coolant or Gas?

blocks.p: Check the color before you clean. Brown to black and thick is engine oil; red or pink is usually automatic transmission or power steering fluid; watery green, orange or pink is coolant; dark and sticky near the wheels may be grease or gear oil.
These behave like light oils, so the same methods work, and a degreaser lifts their reddish tint from concrete well.
Scrape grease off with a plastic putty knife before absorbent and degreaser can reach it. Gear oil carries a sulfur smell that lingers until the oil is gone.
Ethylene glycol tastes sweet and is toxic to pets and children. Absorb it, scrub with soap and water, rinse thoroughly and keep animals away until dry. It rarely leaves a lasting stain.

Gasoline evaporates quickly but softens asphalt and can leave a ring. Absorb it, ventilate, keep sparks away and let it evaporate before washing. Most brake fluid is glycol-based rather than petroleum, and it can strip paint and soften some sealers; absorb it and clean with soap and water.
Any leak that keeps coming back means parking over a drip pan until the car is repaired, because no cleaning routine keeps up with an active leak.

sections.h: How Do You Keep Oil Stains Off Your Driveway?

blocks.p: Catch the drips, seal the surface and keep a spill kit within reach.

A drip pan or containment mat under the engine catches the slow leaks behind most driveway stains. Place it where the engine actually sits when you park, often a foot or two forward of where people guess, and empty it every few weeks.

On asphalt, a fresh coat every two to three years fills surface voids and gives oil less to grab, though oil spots still need priming first. Our guide to [when to seal a new asphalt driveway](/when-should-you-seal-a-new-asphalt-driveway/) covers timing on fresh pavement. On concrete, a penetrating sealer reduces absorption without changing the look; see our [concrete driveway sealer reviews](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/).

Aggressive spot cleaning on concrete strips years of general grime along with the oil, leaving a pale spot. Wash the whole slab with a general cleaner and a surface cleaner to even out the color; our [best driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) picks cover that job.
Keep a bag of absorbent, a stiff brush and a bottle of degreaser by the garage door. Most permanent stains started as spills that sat over a weekend because nothing was on hand.

mistakes: Petroleum solvents, citrus solvents and brake cleaner dissolve asphalt binder as readily as they dissolve oil. The stain may fade while the pavement under it turns soft and ravels. On asphalt, use water-based degreasers, soap and enzyme cleaners labeled asphalt-safe.
Water floats oil and carries it outward, turning a plate-sized stain into a streak and washing oil toward the street drain. Lay down absorbent and grind it in before any water touches the spot.
Calling It Done While the Surface Is Wet

Wet concrete darkens evenly and masks the oil still in it, so many people stop after one round only to see the stain back the next morning. Give the area a full day to dry before deciding on another round or a different product.
Holding the Pressure Washer Too Close

A zero or 15 degree tip a few inches from the surface can etch concrete and strip aggregate from asphalt, leaving a pale, rough patch more visible than the stain. Use a wider tip, stay a foot away on asphalt and keep the wand moving.

Neither asphalt sealer nor concrete sealer bonds well to oil, so coating over a stain often brings peeling or a dark spot bleeding through within a season. Clean the spot, let it dry fully, and on asphalt brush on an oil spot primer before sealing.
bottomLine: Treat the two driveway surfaces differently and most oil stains come out. On asphalt, absorb quickly and stay with dish soap, water-based degreasers and enzyme cleaners, because the pavement is made from the same family of chemicals as the stain. On concrete, absorb quickly, then use a strong alkaline degreaser and a firm scrub, and judge only when dry. A concrete stain that survives two full rounds needs a poultice or enzyme treatment. Once the surface is clean and dry, seal it, put a drip pan under the leak and keep a spill kit by the garage.

faqs.q: How do you remove oil stains from a driveway fast?
faqs.a: Cover the spill with clay kitty litter, grind it in with your shoe and leave it overnight, then scrub the spot with dish soap or a water-based degreaser on asphalt, or an alkaline degreaser on concrete, and rinse. A fresh spill usually comes out in one evening plus about 30 minutes of cleaning the next day.

faqs.q: Does kitty litter really work on driveway oil?
faqs.a: Yes, on fresh spills on both asphalt and concrete. Plain clay litter soaks up free oil well, especially when you grind it in so the granules crumble and reach into the surface texture. It does little for an old, set-in stain, because by then the oil has moved below the surface where litter cannot reach it.

faqs.q: Is dish soap safe on an asphalt driveway?
faqs.a: Yes. Grease-cutting dish soap is one of the safest cleaners for blacktop because it is water-based and leaves the asphalt binder alone. Use plenty, scrub with a nylon brush, wait about 15 minutes and rinse well. It handles fresh and light stains; heavier ones usually call for a water-based degreaser or an enzyme cleaner.

faqs.q: How do you remove oil stains from an asphalt driveway without damaging it?
faqs.a: Absorb the free oil first, then use only water-based cleaners such as dish soap, an asphalt-safe degreaser or an enzyme cleaner, with a nylon brush and short contact times. Avoid solvents, gasoline and wire brushes. If you pressure wash, use a 25 or 40 degree tip at least 12 inches away and keep it moving.

faqs.q: Will oil stains damage asphalt permanently?
faqs.a: They can. Oil softens asphalt binder, and a stain left for weeks can leave a patch that stays tacky or crumbles. Small spots that get cleaned usually recover once primed with an oil spot primer and sealed. Larger soft areas should be cut out and filled with cold patch asphalt before you seal the driveway.

faqs.q: Is it safe to rinse oil cleaner into the street?
faqs.a: Generally not. In most areas storm drains empty untreated into streams and lakes, and many local codes ban washing automotive fluids or degreaser residue into them. Rinse onto gravel or lawn where allowed, or collect the wash water with a wet vacuum and take it to your household hazardous waste program.

faqs.q: Should you clean the whole driveway after removing an oil stain?
faqs.a: Often, on concrete. Spot degreasing can leave a lighter patch because it strips years of grime along with the oil. Washing the whole slab with a driveway cleaner and a surface cleaner attachment evens the color. On asphalt, sealing the driveway after spot cleaning does the same job and protects the pavement too.
